headline: I was one of the 5,000 special guests at the Red Fort, but I spent the entire morning trying to find a power outlet for my portable steamer
body:
When I received my invitation to join the special guests at the Red Fort for Independence Day, I naturally assumed the most important part of my duty was looking sharp. I spent weeks preparing, but I hadn't accounted for the sheer humidity and the lack of a proper grooming station in the VVIP enclosure. 

About halfway through the national anthem, I found myself crouched behind a decorative potted plant, desperately searching for an electrical socket to plug in my portable garment steamer. My kurta had developed a single, persistent wrinkle near the shoulder that I felt was, frankly, an insult to the historic gravity of the venue. 

An usher approached me, looking rather confused as I stood there holding a steaming wand, and asked if I was reporting a fire. I explained that I was simply ensuring my silhouette remained impeccable for the post-ceremony photo ops. He didn't seem to understand that history doesn't just need to be witnessed—it needs to be witnessed without a crease in one’s attire.
caption: Living the VVIP life at the Red Fort comes with its own set of pressing challenges. Some things just can't be left to chance, or wrinkles. #IndependenceDay #RedFort #VVIPProblems #DelhiDiaries (satire)
